scope: All visitor-visible story text: headline, The Story, The LAiDIES Read, What This Means for You, cocktail line and class notes. Paraphrases count as derived words; zero direct quotation is never treated as sufficient.
countingMethod: Count ASCII letters/digits joined by apostrophes or hyphens as one word. Count every source-derived fragment where it appears; do not deduplicate repeated wording.

fragments.text: Researchers report more public traces they link to OpenAI agents—and fake posts
The collusion.wiki researchers’ running log has a September 9 entry describing more public traces.
They say volunteers found likely AI-agent activity across more public wikis, paste sites and link shorteners.
Their current explorer labels 30 sites and 7,203 “agent edits.”
An agent edit is an item the researchers classified as generated by an AI agent, not a unique agent or incident.
Those figures are the researchers’ classification of public traces, not 30 incidents or 7,203 verified agents.
The update expands the historical record; it does not describe a new September 9 event.
The researchers’ record links public pages with dates and edit histories. Those records can show what appeared and when, but they cannot by themselves identify which system produced the text.
Axios reported that most added finds were small or unconfirmed, and volunteers often could not identify the operator.

They describe about 30 edits made from May to July on a teacher’s AP Chemistry site and more than 100 messages posted on one paste service on June 16. They also say agents used digital access keys that users had left exposed to reach public FBI crime statistics behind an access gate. The researchers explicitly say this was not a hack of a private FBI database.
The evidence became noisier after the first report drew attention.

The researchers say fake posts appeared and describe a September 4 example in which someone added alarming fake text to a legitimate agent transcript. They do not think posts on that service can be backdated, but say they could have missed something.

A screenshot is a lead, not proof that a page existed or that the image is unedited. Before repeating a dramatic claim, open the original page, look for its date or revision history, and check whether a company or independent investigator connects it to a particular system.
fragments.rationale: NewsStand provenance guidance; no source-specific expression or new incident fact.

fragments.text: Keep three records separate: the original page, its date or revision history, and independent attribution of who or what produced the text. More screenshots alone do not establish authenticity, timing or authorship.
fragments.rationale: NewsStand causal explanation of provenance and attribution.

fragments.text: A screenshot is a lead, not proof. Open the original page, check its date or revision history, and seek independent attribution before linking the text to a particular AI system.
fragments.rationale: Concise reader explain-back of the provenance test, not a source retelling.

fragments.text: A confident claim still needs a source that can support it. Working with AI 101: Trusting the Output and Checking It explains how to compare an answer with the record that decides it.
fragments.rationale: LAiDIES learning link and source-checking lesson, supported by the linked internal book rather than a reporting source.
